subject: arcadeCabinet

Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.

spec.name: Neon Runner Arcade Cabinet
spec.description: A 1980s upright arcade cabinet in synthwave style: black body with glowing pink and cyan T-molding, a sunset, grid and mountain side-art, a lit marquee, a CRT screen showing a neon road scene, a joystick and button deck, and a glowing coin door.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints. Real size: about 0.7 m wide, 1.85 m tall, 1.03 m deep from the back (z=-0.45) to the control-panel lip (z=+0.58). Facing +Z, from the front down: a lit marquee box on top (y 1.6-1.85), then a CRT bezel and glass leaning back about 8 degrees (y 1.05-1.6), then a control deck sticking out in front at waist height (y 0.86-1.04, z 0.2-0.58). Below the deck is the vertical front board with the coin door (y 0.04-0.92, front face z=0.35). The body narrows toward the top rear. The side profile (z,y) is: [-0.45,0.04] [0.35,0.04] [0.35,0.92] [0.24,1.05] [0.16,1.6] [0.2,1.6] [0.2,1.85] [-0.28,1.85] [-0.28,1.15] [-0.45,0.95]. Panels sit at x=+-0.34 (outer faces), 0.02 thick. Four leveler feet touch y=0 and everything else floats above on the sides' bottom edge y=0.04. The look is synthwave: near-black indigo body, neon pink and cyan glowing T-molding along every side-panel edge, a striped sunset over a magenta perspective grid and layered purple mountains on both side panels, hot-pink glow behind the marquee and screen, chrome and brass fittings, and glowing coloured buttons. Every colour is a flat colour from the palette, and details such as stripes, grid lines, stars and lettering are small separate parts seated on the surface. Parts must not overlap except at shared mount faces. Neon and lit items (T-molding, marquee panel, screen scene, buttons, coin slot lights, start buttons) use the glow kit.

parts.builds: The structural body, built with extrudes, slabs and boxes. (1) Two side panels as extrudes of the side profile above, drawn along z with y up, thickness 0.02, at x=+-0.34 (centres x=+-0.33), colour cabinetBlack. (2) A back panel closing the rear between the sides, following the back profile from y=0.04 to 1.85, with a darker rubber-coloured access door outline, two small steel screws and a vent slot grille of 6 thin rubber slats near the top. (3) A bottom plate and a top plate (top at y=1.85, from z=-0.28 to 0.2) in cabinetBlack, plus a thin deepIndigo inner shelf under the deck. (4) Glowing T-molding: thin neonPink tubes about 0.012 radius following the whole outline of each side panel's outer edge, offset 0.012 outward past the panel face. Use a neonCyan tube along the front vertical edge of the lower body (z=0.35, y 0.04-0.92) on each side, and short neonCyan corner caps at each turn. Glow them at strength 1.5. (5) Four chrome leveler feet (small cylinders, r=0.025) under the corners at y 0-0.04, each with a rubber pad, resting on y=0. (6) Faint deepIndigo trim ribs where the front board meets the sides. Does not cover the side art, front board, deck or marquee.
parts.attaches: Side panels carry sideArt on their outer faces (x=+-0.34, art sits at 0.341+). The front board owned by coinFront fits between the sides at frontBoardFace. The deck sits on sideProfileFront and the sides' step at y 0.92. The bezel and marquee of screenMarquee fit between the sides at bezelBottom and bezelTop.

parts.builds: Synthwave side-art decals, identical on both sides and mirrored with s=+-1, as thin extrudes (thickness about 0.004) seated at x=+-0.343 on the outer side-panel faces, within z from -0.4 to 0.3 and y 0.12 to 1.75, avoiding the T-molding edge by 0.03. Layers from back to front: a deepIndigo backing plate following the panel's inner outline; a big sun disc (radius about 0.24 centred around z=-0.05, y=1.0) as stacked slices, yellow at the top, then orange, then sunsetRed at the bottom, with horizontal cabinetBlack stripe gaps that widen toward the bottom; two layers of mountain silhouettes (mountainMid behind, mountainDark in front, jagged sharp-cornered outlines) along a horizon at y=0.7, with thin neonCyan highlight lines on the peaks; below the horizon a perspective grid in gridMagenta made of thin rods, with converging lines meeting at a vanishing point at the horizon and about 6 horizontal lines spaced closer toward the horizon, sitting on a cabinetBlack ground plate; a small stylised wireframe low-poly palm silhouette on each side, using mountainDark with neonPink trunk stripes; scattered star dots (tiny spheres, white and neonCyan, about 20 each side) in the sky area; a neonPink stripe pair and a neonCyan stripe running diagonally beneath the sun; and a title decal text 'NEON RUNNER' in neonCyan lettering built from thin rods or an svg texture near the top. Sun, grid lines, stripes and stars are glow-ready (strength about 0.6 on the sun and stars).
parts.attaches: Sits flat on the outer faces of cabinetShell's side panels at sideFaceX (x=+-0.341 to +-0.348). It does not cross the front edge of the profile.

parts.builds: The control panel that sticks out in front, from z=0.2 to 0.58, y 0.86 to 1.04, spanning x=+-0.35. A slab with a top surface slightly sloped (about 6 degrees, higher at the back, y=1.02 at deckBackEdge down to y=0.96 at the front lip), a panelPurple top with a rounded-looking bevelled front lip in cabinetBlack and a chrome edge strip along the lip. Top-surface overlay: a thin neonPink outline frame around the player 1 area, small neonCyan stripe chevrons and a 'PLAYER 1' label made of small blocks. Left, a joystick at joystickBase: a chrome dish ring, a rubber base boot, a steel shaft, and a red ball top (r about 0.022) with a small white highlight. Right, at buttonRowCenter, a cluster of 6 chunky arcade buttons in two rows of three (each a cylinder rim in rubber, a coloured cap in buttonRed, buttonBlue, buttonGreen, buttonYellow, neonPink and neonCyan, with a small white highlight on each) glowing at strength 1. In the middle two small round Start buttons (1P in buttonGreen and 2P in buttonYellow) with tiny labels. A trackball with a chrome ring and a dark-red sphere on the left of the joystick is optional. Under the lip, a cabinetBlack apron panel with 3 neonCyan thin accent lines running along the full width. Side cheeks of cabinetBlack at x=+-0.35 close the deck's ends, with neonPink T-molding along the lip's front edge.
parts.attaches: Back edge meets the bezel bottom at deckBackEdge/bezelBottom. Underside rests on the front board top (y 0.92) at z 0.2-0.35. Sides are flush with the cabinet sides at x=+-0.35.

parts.builds: Everything from y=1.05 up at the front. (1) The CRT bezel: a cabinetBlack front board leaning back about 8 degrees between bezelBottom (y=1.05, z=0.24) and bezelTop (y=1.6, z=0.16), with a rectangular opening centred at screenCenter around 0.5 wide by 0.4 high. Built from four frame bars, the flared inner bevel in panelPurple, and a thin neonPink glowing inner trim around the glass. Four small steel screws at the corners. (2) The screen glass: a slightly curved-looking slab of screenGlass at screenCenter facing screenNormal, carrying a glowing synthwave game scene as flat parts in layers, lit with the glow kit. A screenSky background with a horizontal gradient made of 5 bands going from screenSky up through neonViolet and screenGlow at the horizon; a sun semicircle in sunYellow and sunOrange with stripe gaps; a dark mountain line; a ground of cabinetBlack with a gridMagenta perspective road converging to the horizon, two neonCyan road edges and a dashed center line; a small retro low-poly car at the bottom seen from behind, with neonPink body, a cabinetBlack window and two red tail lights; and score text 'SCORE 009900' and 'HI 099999' at the top in white, plus a row of 3 tiny car icons for lives. (3) A shaded CRT hood: sloped cabinetBlack top and side blinders between the bezel and the marquee. (4) The marquee box on top: a cabinetBlack frame (x +-0.34, y 1.6-1.85, front face z=0.21) with a glowing lit title panel 0.6 wide by 0.2 high, a deepIndigo backing with a neonPink to neonViolet to neonCyan horizontal banded gradient, the lettering 'NEON RUNNER' in white with neonCyan shadow offset (as svg texture or letter blocks), a small sun-and-grid emblem on each side of the title, and neonPink outline tubes around the marquee front. (5) Two small speaker grille bars in rubber with chrome slots on either side of the marquee panel.
parts.attaches: Bezel bottom meets the controlDeck back edge at bezelBottom. Bezel and marquee sides tuck between cabinetShell's side panels and follow the side profile. The marquee top is flush with the shell top plate at y=1.85.

parts.builds: The lower front of the cabinet, below the deck, from y=0.04 to 0.92, owning the front board between the side panels at z=0.33-0.35. (1) A cabinetBlack front board with a deepIndigo inset panel. (2) The coin door centred at coinDoorCenter: a chrome-bordered steel door plate (about 0.26 wide by 0.4 high, 0.02 thick, raised to z=0.37) with two coin mechanism modules side by side. Each has a rubber housing, a chrome coin slot plate with a dark slot, a glowing coin button (buttonRed and buttonBlue, glow strength 1.2) with a small '25c' label built from small blocks, and a return cup opening in rubber with a chrome flap. A brass lock cylinder with a keyhole at the door's lower centre. Four tiny steel bolts at the door corners. (3) Below the coin door, a cash-box door plate, rectangular and cabinetBlack, with a chrome handle bar and a brass keyed lock. (4) Neon accents: a neonCyan glowing strip along the door's top border and a neonPink horizontal stripe pair across the full front below the deck (y about 0.88-0.9), with a short row of 5 neonViolet vertical glowing slits at the bottom, each 0.02 wide. (5) A kick-plate toe band at y 0.04-0.14, rubber coloured with a neonPink thin line on top. (6) A small sticker-style sign plate 'INSERT COIN' in white on neonPink above the door, plus a small panel '1 PLAY = 25c'.
parts.attaches: Fits between the shell's side panels at frontBoardFace (z=0.35). Its top meets the underside of controlDeck at y=0.92. Its bottom stops at y=0.04 over the shell's bottom plate.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out dimensions for a 1980s synthwave arcade cabinet—roughly 0.7m wide, 1.85m tall, 0.9m deep, facing forward with a protruding control panel, kept as a static model with no joints.

I'm planning the side profile from the kickplate base up through the sloped control panel, angled monitor bezel, and top marquee, with synthwave-style side art like sunset stripes, grid lines, and extruded mountain shapes. I'm breaking the cabinet into five parts: the cabinet shell with feet and trim, side art, the control deck with joystick and buttons, a screen assembly combining the monitor and marquee, and a coin door section for the front lower area.

Continuing to map out the side profile coordinates, stepping up through the monitor bezel to the marquee top, then tracing the sloped back panel down toward the base.

Now I'm defining the shell's bounding box with small leveler feet raising it off the floor, then placing mount points for the control deck and screen—including the tilted screen plane angled back about 12 degrees with its glass dimensions and center position.

Working out more coordinates for the marquee, coin door, side art panels, and the control deck's trimmed bounding box, then sizing the monitor region nested between the side panels.

I'm deciding how to split ownership between the shell and the screen assembly—shell handles side panels, back, base, top, and interior fillers, while the screen part handles the bezel front, glass, marquee, and CRT hood interior, with the bezel recessed and slightly tilted where it meets the sides.

Now I'm working out the exact side profile coordinates, mapping points from the base up through the control deck, the bezel slope, and into the marquee top, then computing the tilt plane for the screen using two of those key points.

Next I'm defining the marquee as a glowing backlit box above the cabinet, positioning the "NEON RUNNER" text panel, and figuring out the slight overhang at the front face.

Then I turn to the coin door assembly: placing a front panel with a recessed coin door unit around mid-height, featuring two lit coin slots and return flaps, with a cash door and lock below, deciding whether the shell or the coin-door part should own the lower front board and kickplate.

Next I plan the side art as a separate panel at the outer faces, layered with a sunset gradient sun, horizon grid, mountain silhouette, stars, palms, and possibly a title decal, with T-molding trim owned by the shell—all while keeping the total part count within budget before moving on to designing the control deck.

I settle on shell dimensions with the deck spanning slightly proud of the sides, adding T-molding thickness to the overall size. I'm tallying part budgets across the shell, side art, control deck, marquee, and coin front to stay within limits, then starting to define a compact neon-themed color palette for the cabinet.

Counting back up, I land on exactly 24 colors, dropping palmGreen and using mountainDark for palm silhouettes instead. Now I'm outlining the full spec with mount details, build notes on glow effects for neon/screen/marquee elements, no joints, and confirming text-bearing SVG works fine before writing the final JSON.

I'm planning out a static buildCabinetShell function that uses the extrude, part, sweep, and glow kit utilities, relying on the Ctx type already provided by the module rather than importing it myself.

Working out the thickness direction gives -x, so the side panels sit centered at their offset positions. I'm checking the side profile points to confirm there's no self-intersection, noting the notch near the top mimics a CRT's slanted back, and setting up the side panels at x=±0.33 with 0.02 thickness using the outline's origin at that offset.

Now I'm placing the neon T-molding tube along the panel's outer edge, trying to pick a centre offset around 0.35 with a 0.012 radius so it slightly overlaps the side art at the boundary without drifting too far outward.

For the corners, I'm deciding to sweep each edge as its own capsule segment with round caps rather than one closed polyline, since the capsule ends can overlap neatly at the joints for a smooth look. I'll use about 10 segments per side (20 capsules total), keeping the front vertical edge cyan instead of pink to match the color scheme.

I'll accept some overlap near the deck cheeks and just end the cyan molding around y=0.92 rather than trying to perfectly trim it. For the glow effect, I'm confirming the capsule sweep mesh works fine with the glow function since materials clone per color. Now moving on to the back panel profile.

For the back panel, I'm mapping out the polygon shape from the profile points and building it as three separate slabs matching the vertical, slanted, and upper vertical sections of that profile.

Working out the outward normal direction for the slanted board, then nudging its center slightly inward along that normal so the box's thickness axis aligns correctly with the slope.

Now I'm computing the exact box dimensions and centers for the upper and lower back panels, making sure their back faces land flush at the correct z-depth to match the slanted profile edges.

I'll add a thin inner shelf under the deck, keeping it within the cabinet bounds. Then I'm considering the back access door—a rubber-colored plate with an outlined frame positioned just outside the back panel.

Still detailing door hardware...

Now I'm placing the vent grille plate with its rubber slats on the upper back panel, and working through the lower access door position on the outer face. I'm also adding chrome feet at the base corners, each with a small rubber pad and chrome stem for grounding contact.

Bottom plate runs 0.04-0.06 with feet topping out at 0.04, using 8-segment cylinders. Now I'm positioning thin deepIndigo trim ribs where the front board meets the sides, placing them just in front of the board edge near x ±0.31 to avoid overlapping geometry.

I'm finalizing the rib placement at x ±0.31, z around 0.354, protruding slightly for visual depth, and considering whether to add cyan corner cap spheres at the front lower edge turn points, staying mindful of the 150-part budget.

Mapping out the vertex coordinates...

I realize the tube radius means the molding centerline needs to sit inset from the panel edges rather than exactly on them, so I'm checking whether the top/bottom tubes stick out past the floor or marquee boundary and whether the side tube centers fall outside the panel face.

Writing polygon offset logic...

Checking that the front vertical cyan edge and corner caps align with the inset vertices without colliding with the leveler foot, and setting glow strength to 1.5 for the pink and cyan capsules.

I'm adding a small sphere cap part with glow applied. I'm considering an inner liner panel for the cabinet side but deciding it would be hidden from view, so I'll skip it along with the edge lip bevel.

Now I'm thinking through back-panel extras: a power inlet box with a switch near the lower right, a tiny rear sticker label, and maybe a warning stripe accent, while skipping top plate vents and bottom plate details since they won't add visible value. Interior CRT detailing and rear bracing structure aren't necessary either.

I'm also weighing small door hinges, a chrome handle bar, and a back seam trim strip along board joints, then settling on a final palette (cabinetBlack, rubber, deepIndigo, neonPink, neonCyan, chrome, steel, white, panelPurple) and roughing out part counts starting with the sides and tubes.

Tallying the rest of the pieces now: pink/cyan segments and caps, back boards, door frame with panel and hinges and handle and screws, vent plate and slats, top/bottom/shelf plates, feet, ribs, and the power box, landing around 95 parts total, with maybe a few extra screws around the back corners for detail. Now I'm setting up the extrude function call with its color parameter...

Writing screw cylinder code...

Now I'm working out the door geometry—positioning the recessed panel and the raised frame bars around it so the panel sits flush inside the border with matching proportions.

Then I'm placing the handle: a vertical chrome bar at the door's right edge connected by two small posts spanning from the panel face out to the bar, nudging the depths slightly to avoid gaps or overlaps.

Now I'm adding the hinges as steel boxes straddling the left frame edge at three vertical positions, and starting to place small corner screws on the panel near the frame bar.

Next I'm working out the power inlet placement on the lower board, positioning a steel plate with an inset rubber socket and small chrome switch near the bottom edge of the panel.

I'm also placing a warning sticker with a neon pink strip above the inlet, then laying out a vent assembly on the upper board — a backing plate with six stacked rubber slats spaced evenly along its height.

Adding corner screws, checking the bevel on the side panel extrusion for a cleaner silhouette, and considering small finishing touches like chrome leveler feet and top plate trim.

Now I'm working out the bottom and top plate dimensions so they don't overlap with the back and front boards, adjusting the z-ranges and centers to fit cleanly against the lower board's height and position.

I'm also placing the upper board above it and checking that it touches the top plate correctly at the seams, while accepting a slight overlap at the slanted board's ends since it's minor. Then I'm positioning the shelf board underneath the deck, aligning its depth to fit beneath the deck surface.

Now I'm adding support cleats on both inner sides beneath the shelf to hold it in place, then moving on to writing the actual component code with the color palette and a profile-based polygon offset function to generate the rounded case geometry.

Writing offset polygon logic...

I'm computing the offset for the slanted board's inward edge to avoid overlap, centering it at the right position, and deciding to skip extra decorative details like screws or seams to keep things simple. Now I'll finalize the geometry, adding small cyan caps at the inner vertices using mirrored positions for the front verticals.

I'm planning to implement buildCoinFront using the given Ctx signature without importing its type, relying on it being in scope. Since this is a static model, I can skip joints entirely and just build the geometry directly in model space using box parts.

I'm importing the glow kit and sticking mostly to the palette colors, with a few custom dark tones for the slot and accents. Then I'm laying out the front face piece by piece: the coin board centered between the side panels, a pair of thin neon pink stripes near the top for the deck underside, and a door region with an "INSERT COIN" sign plate positioned just above it.

I'm figuring out placement for the "1 PLAY = 25c" panel and a cyan strip along the door's top border, working out x and y coordinates so everything fits within the board's width without overlapping the door.

Now I need a small pixel font for the text, sketching 3x5 block glyphs for each letter and number required.

Given that "INSERT COIN" alone would mean too many individual box parts, I'm planning to merge the geometries per color using BufferGeometryUtils instead, keeping the part budget manageable while still letting each letter render as boxes in local space.

Defining the pixel font...

I'm working out the text orientation so letters read correctly for a viewer facing the model, with the glyph columns increasing toward +X. Then I'm positioning the door geometry, placing a chrome-bordered steel plate slightly inset within a larger chrome frame centered on the door.

Adding a glowing cyan strip above the frame, then laying out the door contents: a steel plate surface with two rubber-housed modules placed side by side and a lock cylinder positioned near the bottom center.

Within each module I'm positioning a chrome coin slot plate at the top, a glowing button beneath it with a "25¢" label, and a coin return cup with an angled chrome flap at the bottom.

Adding the chrome ring behind the button cap oriented along the z-axis, then laying out the return cup opening and chrome flap details at slightly different depths and tilts for visual layering.

I'm also placing corner bolts and screws on the steel door plate, keeping them clear of the module housings, plus starting on a brass lock cylinder detail.

Working out the lock assembly with a chrome ring, keyhole slot, and surrounding geometry, checking that it sits below the module housing without overlapping the return cups.

I'm also deciding whether to skip a backing plate under the door and instead planning the vertical zones of the front panel, starting with a rubber toe band at the bottom with a pink accent line above it.

For the five glowing neon violet slits, I'm placing them directly on that toe band rather than between it and the cash box door, spacing them evenly and keeping them short and narrow so they read as a subtle glowing row near the base.

Now I'm working out the layering depths for the cash box front: the deep indigo panel gets inset from the main board, the pink stripe sits above it, and the door plate and bars need to sit flush on that inset face rather than overlapping it, so I'm recalculating the z-depths for each layer to stack correctly from the board outward.

I'm adding a chrome handle bar with standoffs, a brass keyed lock, corner screws, and a thin steel border frame for the cash door, then moving on to position the neon pink "INSERT COIN" sign plate.

For the sign, I'm keeping it unlit flat neonPink with white pixel text sized to fit the plate, plus a dark cabinetBlack backing frame slightly larger than the pink plate to give it a bordered sticker look.

Now I'm sizing a second panel reading "1 PLAY = 25c" in purple, adjusting pixel size down to 0.0022 so the text fits within the 0.12 wide panel near the door's right edge.

Defining chevron polygon points...

I'm placing three chevrons side by side near the door frame, then adding a pink neon stripe pair near the top of the board with a cyan glow matching the door's top border strip.

I'll skip extra violet framing around the inset panel to avoid clutter, keeping the part count near 60, and instead add a rubber kick plate toe band along the bottom front edge of the board.

Working out the slit housing dimensions and spacing for the glowing LED strip, then positioning the front board centered between the side panels with a small clearance gap.

I'm also adding hinge barrel cylinders to the door's left edge, carefully adjusting their x-position and radius so they sit flush against the frame without overlapping.

Now I'm thinking through the glow effects: importing the glow kit for flat-colored merged parts and buttons, and adding small glowing accent lights beside the coin slot to frame it with a subtle rim light.

I'm defining small helper functions for creating box and cylinder parts, including orientation handling so cylinders can be aimed along different axes.

Now I'm building a simple bitmap text renderer, mapping characters to pixel font rows and scanning each row for runs of filled pixels to generate geometry for the letters.

I'm layering the sign's z-depths for the frame, pink plate, cyan shadow, and white text so they stack cleanly without overlapping, giving the "INSERT COIN" text a subtle offset glow effect.

Now I'm placing the "25c" module label on the housing top with white text sized to fit within the housing width, while skipping extra decorative details like screws or colored underlines to keep things simple.

For the slot plate, I'm adding a chrome base layer with a darker recessed slot box above it, checking the z-depths line up so the slot sits just above the plate surface. Then I'm adding yellow glowing slot light bars positioned symmetrically within the housing bounds, making sure they clear the plate edges, before moving on to defining the button ring.

Working out the flap rotation direction so the hinge stays at top and the bottom swings outward toward +z — settling on roughly -15° to keep the extents small. I'm skipping extra details like a coin lamp and moving on to placing the cash door plate on the cabinet, centered around (0, 0.24, 0.357) at 0.3x0.12 size.

Now I'm building the surrounding steel border bars, handle standoffs, and bar cylinder for the cash door, working out their exact positions and dimensions relative to the plate.

Adding a "CASH" label in steel-colored text near the handle, then placing four hex bolts at the corners of the cash door plate, and setting up corner bolt positions for the door itself.

I'm double-checking that bolt positions don't overlap the housing or frame edges, confirming the cyan top strip sits just above the frame's top bar without colliding with it.

Now I'm computing exact coordinates for the frame bars (top, bottom, sides) and the inner plate dimensions, making sure depth and height values are consistent with the steel door plate, then considering whether to add recessed groove details for visual texture.

I'm also planning smaller hardware details—hinge barrels, a chrome latch near the door edge, and thin violet glow lines along the inset edges for a neon accent—while double-checking they don't overlap the chevron decorations.

Now I'm setting up a small helper function for creating box geometry parts with position and optional rotation, and being careful to only import what's actually used so the build doesn't fail on unused-import checks.

I'm placing two buttons symmetrically, red on the left and blue on the right, with a small gap between their housings, then writing the chevron extrusion outlines and picking glow strengths for the various light elements—stripes brighter at 1.5, slits and chevrons around 1.2—before adding a tiny highlight sphere to each button for shine.

I'm planning the control deck as a static structure with no joints, built directly from parts in model space, and starting to work out the deck geometry dimensions.

Working through the slope calculation for the deck top surface, then thinking through the deck body's extrusion profile—its thickness, side cheeks flush with the cabinet, and how the slab and apron panels fit together underneath.

Computing the sloped core and plate dimensions...

Continuing the lip chamfer profile...

I'll let it seat slightly embedded into the lip since that's a minor soft overlap. Now I'm adding an apron panel hanging below the lip - a thin box roughly 0.67 wide and 0.02 thick positioned under the core, with plans to add three cyan accent lines on it.

Still planning the apron geometry...

Tracing the slope where the shell side profile angles up toward the deck, I realize the cheek placement at x 0.34–0.36 risks overlapping both the side panel and the side art decoration, which sits around z 0.2–0.3, y 0.92–1.02. I'll need to nudge the cheek position or accept slight overlap since the spec calls for it, keeping the art band around 0.341–0.348.

I'm realizing the deck and shell side panel geometry actually overlap in this z-range, since the shell side extends wide enough at z around 0.2-0.35 to intrude on the deck's claimed width. I need to reconcile this by keeping the deck sides flush with the cabinet sides rather than at a fixed offset, rather than treating them as independent shapes.

Working through the cheek geometry placement...

Still placing cheek geometry... I'm adding a small rim where the cheek sits slightly above the top plate, then positioning the neon pink T-molding rod along the lip's front edge beneath the chrome strip, checking it stays within the bounding box.

Now I'm figuring out the cabinet-black apron panel beneath the lip, sizing a thin box to sit flush with the cheek's bottom diagonal chamfer.

Working out the cheek profile coordinates to align with the apron front and lip overhang, aiming for a slight diagonal taper near the top edge.

Now I'm figuring out the top surface orientation: the slope runs at about 8.97° forward, so the normal vector tilts toward positive z, which I need for placing objects flush against the tilted top plate.

I'll build a helper that places geometry on the surface by offsetting along the normal by half the object's height, so cylinders and boxes sit flush against the sloped top. I'll also pull in a glow kit for accents and confirm that color props accept named palette strings like neonPink.

Now I'm working out the actual coordinates: joystick and button positions relative to the surface, computing their y-values from the slope function, and figuring out the bounding frame dimensions for the player-1 control area so an outline can wrap around the joystick and buttons.

Working out the pixel-font sizing for "PLAYER 1" with 0.005 cell size, then figuring out how to merge all the label blocks into one geometry positioned on the tilted surface using tangent vectors and rotation matrices to keep everything aligned to the plane's tilt.

Without a bone specified, parts default to the nearest joint, which is fine for static pieces since there are no joints defined. I'll apply glow to the merged geometry with shared flat-color materials per color string, keeping labels white (non-glowing) and chevrons neon cyan with glow. For the pixel font I need a 3x5 grid covering characters P, L, A, Y, E, R, 1, S, T to spell out labels like "PLAYER 1", "1P", and "2P".

Defining pixel font rows...

Now I'm building a text-rendering function that converts strings into block geometries positioned in 3D space, oriented so the text reads correctly from the player's viewpoint looking from +z toward -z, with the top of the letters facing away from the player.

I'm placing the left joystick on the player's left side and buttons on the right, then starting to model the joystick's chrome dish ring component.

Writing lathe geometry...

Checking the total height against the box limit, I realize I need to shorten the shaft so the ball top stays under 1.12 — adjusting boot, shaft, and ball positions to fit within bounds, then adding a small white highlight sphere on the ball's upper-left-front for shading.

I'm deciding whether to add an optional trackball next to the joystick for extra detail, sketching out its rough position and ring radius.

Now I'm laying out the six-button cluster in two rows of three near the buttonRowCenter, sizing the rubber rims and caps with slight raised lift so they sit naturally in the panel.

Now working out the two button rows (red/blue/green and yellow/pink/cyan) and figuring out placement for the small round Start buttons between the joystick and the button cluster, checking spacing so everything fits without overlapping.

Labeling the Start buttons "1P" and "2P" with centered text underneath, then positioning decorative neon chevron stripes toward the front edge of the deck.
